body:
## Summary

The `s3` role cannot be told what chunk size to use. Every deployed gateway chunks at the 1 MiB default, regardless of workload, hardware, or the D-server fan-out it is fronting.

This is a wiring gap, not a design position. The seam already exists and the sibling role already exposes it:

- `Gateway::with_chunk_size` — `crates/server/src/lib.rs:145`, doc-commented "mainly so tests can force multi-chunk objects", i.e. it exists today as a test affordance.
- `wyrd put --chunk-size N` — parsed at `crates/server/src/cli.rs:555`, threaded through `cluster_store_put` / `local_store_put`.
- `cmd_s3` (`cli.rs:2113`) parses `--s3-listen`, `--data-dir`, `--region`, `--access-key`, `--secret-key`, `--metadata-backend`, `--coordination-backend`, `--endpoints`, `--otlp-endpoint` — and no chunk size. `serve_s3_role` is never given one, so `DEFAULT_CHUNK_SIZE` (`crates/server/src/lib.rs:50`, `1 << 20`) always wins.

## Why it matters

**Operators cannot tune the write path.** Chunk size sets the unit of erasure coding, the fan-out width per object, the metadata chunk-map growth rate, and the peak resident bytes per in-flight PUT (`crates/core/src/write.rs:528` — "peak resident bytes are one `chunk_size` piece plus its ..."). One value cannot be right for a 9-node NVMe fleet and a single-node loopback both.

**It blocks measurement.** The blackbox driver (proposal 0017) sizes its test objects to straddle the chunk boundary deliberately. With chunk size fixed and unexposed, the driver has to assume 1 MiB and its size coverage is accurate only by coincidence. Same for any future throughput work — chunk size is the first knob a `cargo xtask bench` sweep would want.

**The dist package cannot record it.** `deploy/dist/env/s3.env.example` mirrors the blueprint's production invocations. A deployment's chunk size is part of its identity and currently cannot be written down.

## Scope

- Parse `--chunk-size` in `cmd_s3`, defaulting to the current value so existing invocations are unaffected.
- Thread it to `Gateway::with_chunk_size` through `serve_s3_role`, and update that builder's doc comment — it is no longer test-only.
- Add it to the `wyrd s3` usage line (`cli.rs:479` has the `put` equivalent).
- Add it to `deploy/dist/env/s3.env.example` and the `small-multi-node-fdb` compose gateway commands.
- Reject a zero or absurd value at parse time rather than clamping silently (`with_chunk_size` currently does `.max(1)`).

Consider also collapsing the two `DEFAULT_CHUNK_SIZE` definitions — `crates/server/src/lib.rs:50` and `crates/server/src/cli.rs:64`, both `1 << 20` — into one, so role and CLI cannot drift.

## Out of scope

Per-object or per-bucket chunk size. This is one process-level default, matching how every other role knob works today.

## Definition of done

- `wyrd s3 --chunk-size N` is honoured end to end: an object written through the gateway at `N` produces the chunk count `N` implies.
- Default behaviour is byte-identical to today when the flag is absent.
- The env example and compose stack carry the flag.

## Refs

Proposal 0017 §Dependencies · `crates/server/src/lib.rs:50,145` · `crates/server/src/cli.rs:64,479,555,2113` · `crates/core/src/write.rs:528`
